title: The mushroom responsible for most fatal poisonings on Earth #shorts
description: The death cap mushroom looks harmless but contains a toxin with no antidote, responsible for most fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow #mushrooms
script: Did you know a single mushroom cap can be enough to kill an adult? The death cap looks almost ordinary, pale green or white with a smooth rounded cap, easily mistaken for edible varieties by inexperienced foragers. Its toxin, amatoxin, shuts down the liver by blocking protein production in cells, but symptoms don't appear for six to twelve hours, long after the toxin has already spread through the body. By the time nausea sets in, serious damage is often already done, and there is still no reliable antidote. It's responsible for the vast majority of fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide.

title: The octopus mother who starves herself for her eggs #shorts
description: A giant Pacific octopus mother guards her eggs for months without eating, and dies shortly after they finally hatch. #shorts #animals #nature #facts #didyouknow #ocean
script: Did you know an octopus mother will starve herself to death for her own children? The giant Pacific octopus, the largest octopus species alive, lays up to a hundred thousand eggs in a single clutch, then coils around them in a den and refuses to leave, even to hunt. For months, sometimes over half a year, she blows currents of water over the eggs to keep them clean and oxygenated, using up her own body until she visibly wastes away. The moment the eggs finally hatch, her job is done, and within days she dies, having spent her final months entirely for offspring she'll never see grow up.

title: The fish that fishes for other fish #shorts
description: The warty frogfish dangles a wriggling lure from its own head to trick smaller fish into swimming straight into its mouth. #shorts #animals #nature #facts #didyouknow #ocean
script: Did you know a fish can go fishing using its own body as bait? The warty frogfish is covered in lumpy, algae-like skin that lets it sit almost invisible on the seafloor for hours without moving. Above its mouth dangles a modified fin ray called an esca, which it wiggles like a live worm to lure curious fish close. The moment prey gets near enough, the frogfish opens its mouth and swallows in as little as six milliseconds, one of the fastest strikes in the entire animal kingdom, faster than the human eye can even register.

title: The snail that hunts and kills other snails #shorts
description: The assassin snail is a predator that tracks other snails by scent and swallows them whole. #shorts #animals #nature #facts #didyouknow #wildlife
script: Did you know some snails hunt other snails? The assassin snail crawls across the substrate of freshwater streams and ponds, tracking chemical trails left by other snails moving across the mud. Once it catches up, it uses its extendable proboscis to force its way inside the prey's shell, injecting digestive enzymes that dissolve the victim's flesh from the inside. It can take hours to fully consume a single prey snail, and afterward it hides the empty shell nearby. Aquarium keepers now use assassin snails on purpose, to control plagues of smaller pest snails that take over fish tanks.
